podcast.body: Noel Gallagher claimed this as the first good song he wrote for Oasis, with origins tracing back to 1991 when he was working for British Gas in Manchester. After a foot injury, he was reassigned to a parts desk storeroom, a job so undemanding that he began bringing his guitar to work and writing songs. The song took years to develop, starting as a mess of chords and a rough melody. The opening chords were first played repeatedly during soundchecks for Inspiral Carpets. Inspiration struck while listening to The Rolling Stones' "Shine a Light" from "Exile on Main Street," prompting the phrase "maybe I don't really want to know." Noel intended it as an answer to Nirvana's "I Hate Myself and Want to Die," annoyed by Kurt Cobain's misery despite his fame. When presented to the band, they initially disbelieved Noel had written it due to its quality. It was recorded at Clear studio in Manchester and released on August 8, 1994, as the third advance single for "Definitely Maybe," bringing Oasis their first worldwide attention. "He'd later say that Live Forever is supposed to be an answer to the Nirvana song I hate myself and want to die."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The third of five songs from their debut album, *Definitely Maybe*. Noel Gallagher had written this song before taking over his brother's band. It exuded optimism, notably contrasting with the gloom and pessimism of grunge, and Noel was particularly annoyed by Nirvana's "I hate myself and want to die." "Noel Galler had had that song in his back pocket, having written it before he launched his coup and took over his little brother's band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
